summary: mobile-release.yml can publish a sideload APK for app.tn07.switchboard on request. bundletool builds a universal APK from the verified AAB, signs it with the upload key, the verifier checks package, version, signer and checksum, and a separate job with contents write publishes it as the non-latest GitHub release mobile-v<version>. switchboard.tn07.dev/apk already redirects to the newest release with an .apk asset. A new play input lets a dispatch skip the Play upload.

desktop.reason: No desktop code reads mobile releases. The new release is created with --latest=false, so electron-updater keeps resolving the desktop release as latest.

reactNativeIos.reason: apps/mobile is untouched. iOS ships through EAS and mobile-ota.yml, which this change does not touch.

nativeAndroid.reason: apps/android source is untouched. The APK is built from the same AAB that goes to Play, and the app has no in-app updater that could read the new release.

sharedBackendApi.reason: No wire protocol, IPC channel or handler changes.

storageDataMigration.reason: No stored data changes. A sideload install is signed with the upload key and cannot upgrade a Play install or the old app.switchboard.mobile package; docs/releasing.md already says to uninstall first.

automated: tests/unit/android-native-ci.test.ts checks that the APK lane is opt-in, runs after the AAB verifier, is verified itself with --checksum, passes keystore passwords as files, publishes only from a needs-release job with contents write, and never marks the release latest. It also checks that the Play upload is gated on the play input.
notExercised: The workflow has not been dispatched with apk on, so bundletool build-apks with the CI keystore, the verifier on the universal APK, and gh release create have not run in CI yet.
The universal APK has not been installed on a device.
